newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT details sector outlook.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT details sector outlook.

text.p: Dutch paper and packaging group KNP BT said on Friday it expected substantial improvement in its 1997 results compared to 1996, partially due to earlier acquisitions.
Detailing the prospects for its business sectors, KNP BT said it expected packaging to make a satisfactory return in 1997 as long as raw material prices did not rise substantially.
It said corrugated paper companies would have to raise prices in the current second quarter, due to margin pressure.
Producers of corrugated cardboard and solid cardboard packaging would also have to hike prices, because of higher raw material costs, KNP BT said.
The firm said it expected prices for wood-free coated paper to remain under pressure for the rest of 1997, due to additional capacity coming on stream.
KNP said its Austrian Leykam unit would raise its prices for wood-free coated paper in the second quarter.
The company said an extraordinary gain on the sale of its plastic packaging activities to Tenneco Inc would be included in the group's second quarter results.
It said first quarter extraordinary charges related to planned restructurings would partially offset the one-off gain, but said it expected an overall extraordinary gain.

"KNP BT reiterates its earlier forecast that the group's profit, assuming that the paper market does not slow down, will show a substantial improvement in the current year compared to 1996," KNP BT said.
Earlier KNP BT said first quarter 1997 net profit from ordinary operations was 52 million guilders versus 50 million guilders in the same period of 1996.
